scientific_question: For two simultaneously escaping noncompact K5 group variables restricted to a common boost axis with fixed positive relative rapidity, does a conservative source-faithful Toller envelope overcome both radial Haar growth factors on the frozen gamma-simple j=2,5 matrix?

source_basis.predecessor: Iter443 established the one-group source envelope M_j(beta)=max_{m,branch}|t_branch| with asymptotic e^{-beta} scaling on the frozen matrix
source_basis.k5_incidence: For two escaping K5 vertices, each has three edges to the fixed complement and the pair has one mutual edge.
source_basis.common_axis_scope: The two escaping group variables are frozen to the same boost axis, beta1=B+c/2 and beta2=B-c/2, so the mutual relative boost has rapidity c.

required_checks: all source Toller values finite on the frozen matrix
for every frozen c, R2(B,c) is strictly decreasing across B=8,10,12,14
for every frozen c, fitted log R2 versus B slope is <= -1.8
external M_j(beta)*exp(beta) remains asymptotically stable on the frozen beta1/beta2 window

interpretation_rule.absence_or_failure_scope: A failed scoped envelope gate is not by itself a theorem that the causal vertex diverges.

scope_guard: PASS establishes only a conservative two-group common-axis fixed-separation noncompact escape witness on the frozen source matrix. It does not cover the collision strip c->0, arbitrary angular directions, three- or four-group simultaneous escape, full Haar/angular causal-vertex finiteness, generalized causal-vertex normalization, causal-stack cutoff removal, family terminality, D7-S3/S4 closure, terminal D7 authorization, or Candidate Gravity activation.
